items.stem: Why do most atoms form chemical bonds?

options.text: To achieve a stable, full outer electron shell
options.rationale: Correct: atoms bond to reach a stable electron arrangement like the noble gases.
Mass change is not the driver of bonding.
Colour is not why atoms bond.

items.explanation: Correct: atoms bond to reach a stable electron arrangement like the noble gases.

items.stem: Which TWO statements describe ionic bonding? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Electrons are transferred from one atom to another
options.rationale: Correct: ionic bonding involves electron transfer.

options.text: It forms positive and negative ions that attract each other
options.rationale: Correct: oppositely charged ions attract in ionic bonding.
Sharing describes covalent bonding, not ionic.

options.text: It only occurs between two non-metals
options.rationale: Ionic bonding is typically between a metal and a non-metal.

items.explanation: Correct: ionic bonding involves electron transfer.

items.stem: A substance has a low melting point and exists as small separate molecules. Which bonding is most likely?

options.rationale: Correct: simple molecular (covalent) substances have low melting points.
Ionic compounds have high melting points and are not small separate molecules.
The molecules are held together by covalent bonds.

options.text: Bonding that makes it a metal
options.rationale: This describes a simple molecular covalent substance, not a metal.

items.explanation: Correct: simple molecular (covalent) substances have low melting points.
